name: Royyala Iguru
subtitle: prawns cooked dry in a thick masala until it clings to every one

ingredients.qty: 500g medium, shelled and deveined, tails on

prepNotes: Toss the prawns with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and leave them 15 minutes, then rinse and pat them completely dry.
Chop the onion finer than feels necessary — iguru is a dry curry and the masala has to melt into a coating, not sit in lumps.
Have everything cut and measured before you start; from the moment the prawns go in you have four minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai over medium-high heat and fry the onion for 10 minutes, until soft and browning at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves and cook 2 minutes until the garlic loses its raw edge.
Add the tomato and cook 8 minutes, mashing it down, until it is completely broken and the oil starts to show at the sides.
steps.tip: Iguru has no added water, so all the moisture must come out of the tomato now.

steps.text: Stir in the chilli powder, coriander powder, remaining turmeric and crushed pepper and fry 2 minutes on low heat.
Add the salt and cook the masala another 3 minutes until it is thick enough to hold the mark of a spoon.
Raise the heat to high, tip in the dried prawns and stir them through the masala for 3 to 4 minutes, until they curl into loose Cs and turn opaque coral.
steps.tip: Prawns go from tender to rubbery in about 60 seconds. A tight O shape means you have gone too far.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and sprinkle over the garam masala.
Squeeze in the lemon juice, scatter the coriander leaves and toss once.
steps.tip: Lemon off the heat only — boiled, it goes bitter and flat.

storage: Best eaten the day it is made. It keeps 1 day refrigerated; reheat quickly in a hot pan for 90 seconds rather than a slow simmer, which overcooks the prawns. Do not freeze.
